title: Why AI Tools Need Different Testing
description: Explain why non-deterministic output changes what a test can and can't assert — and where the boundary between ordinary software and model judgment actually sits in a real tool.

title: Mocking Claude in Tests
description: Test AI-dependent code without hitting the real API every run — recording real responses, mocking failure modes on purpose, and knowing when a live call in CI is still worth the cost.

title: Debugging Bad Output
description: Find the actual cause of a bad AI response instead of just rewording the prompt — reproducing it first, localizing it to prompt, context, or model, logging enough to debug after the fact, and confirming a fix without breaking three other cases.

title: Handling Edge Cases
description: Find and handle the inputs that break an AI-powered tool before a user finds them — empty, huge, and malformed input, unexpected languages and formats, output that's valid-but-wrong, and adversarial input aimed at the prompt itself.

title: Building an Eval Harness
description: Build a repeatable way to measure whether an AI feature is actually working — a real test set beats a vague sense it's fine, automated scoring where you can get it, sampled human review where you can't, run before every real change to catch a regression before a user does.
